relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.role: Professor of Sanskrit and Indian Antiquities
relations.evidence: Hofrath Dr. J. G. Bühler, C. I. E., Professor of Sanskrit and Indian Antiquities in the University of Vienna, had met his death by drowning in Lake Constance.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: He was a student at the University of Göttingen where he took his doctor's degree in 1858.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: His master was the famous linguist and folklorist Theodor Benfey, and Benfey was always very proud of his pupil

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: held for a short time the post of Assistant Librarian at the Royal Library in Windsor.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: After three years he returned to Göttingen, to take up an appointment at the University Library.

relations.subject: M. A. Stein
relations.evidence: was undoubtedly fostered by Bühler, in his turn among pupils such as Dr. M. A. Stein, who has done such valuable archæological work in Kashmir.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: At Easter, 1855, he proceeded to the University of Göttingen to study Classical and Oriental antiquities, and found there such eminent teachers as Hermann Sauppe, Ernst Curtius, Theodor Benfey, and Heinrich Ewald.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.evidence: he was invited to take the newly created chair of Oriental languages at the Elphinstone College in Bombay. Bühler gladly accepted the offer, and began his work at Bombay in the spring of 1863.

relations.subject: Johann Georg Bühler
relations.role: co-compiler of Digest of Hindu Law
relations.evidence: As early as 1864 Bühler, together with Sir Raymond West, then judge at the Bombay High Court, was appointed by the Governor of Bombay Presidency, to compile a Digest of Hindu Law
